title: Curated usage ontology and analytics surface for Console telemetry
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Build a curated analytics surface that standardizes Console telemetry into an explicit usage ontology and a set of production-ready materialized tables for downstream reporting, billing reconciliation, and model/perf SLO attribution. The piece will sit on top of existing event ingestion and sessionization pipelines and provide denormalized, query-optimized tables alongside clear schema contracts

Scope:
- Define an event taxonomy (actions, route types, actor types, artifact types) and mapping rules from raw callstream and console events.
- Implement dbt models to generate: a) user_journey_sessions (session-level canonical view), b) invocation_enriched (per-invocation denorm with route, model_variant, latency, token_counts), c) org_daily_telemetry_rollup (cost/latency/failure aggregates), and d) feature_exposure_facts (flag exposures per-session).
- Materialize tables into Delta/Parquet with partitioning by org_id and date and with compaction strategy documented.
- Add lineage metadata and table-level tags for retention and sensitivity.
- Provide a backwards-compatible schema evolution plan and migration steps for downstream consumers.

Why now: Multiple product and finance stakeholders requested canonical tables for SLA dashboards, cost attribution experiments, and to reduce repeated ad-hoc joins and expensive queries on raw event stores. This will reduce query latency and costs and create a stable contract for Console dashboards and the billing audit pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Event taxonomy documented and reviewed by PM and Design (Confluence link)
dbt models merged to analytics repo with tests (unique keys, not-null, and schema tests)
Materialized tables exist in prod dataset with partitioning and sample queries meeting latency targets (< 3s for common slices)
Data freshness SLA: daily refresh completed within 4 hours of midnight UTC; ad-hoc nearline for last 6 hours for operational dashboards
Downstream consumers (Console dashboards, billing job, model-eval) confirm parity/acceptance
Migration notes and roll-back steps published in repo and Confluence
work_items: Finalize event taxonomy and mapping rules (owner: Daniel)
Write dbt models for canonical session and invocation tables (owner: Daniel)
Add tests and CI for dbt models; incremental materialization strategy
Create table-level ACLs and retention tags; coordinate with Security/Compliance
Run perf benchmarks on sample partitions and tune partitioning/compaction
Publish Confluence PRD and announce ownership to analytics consumers
Coordinate with infra to schedule nightly compaction and optimize query concurrency
decisions: Canonical storage: Delta Lake (Parquet) on our analytics S3 bucket; use date and org_id partitioning
Materialization: dbt incremental models with periodic full-refresh window for first 30 days
Primary session boundary: 30 minutes of user inactivity + explicit sign-out events
Join keys: use invocation_id and session_id as primary logical joins to preserve denorm efficiency
Schema evolution: add columns as nullable with feature flags; major changes require migration plan and consumer sign-off
risks: Raw event schema churn from upstream producers causing dbt test failures and pipeline flakiness
Large orgs produce hot partitions (high-volume org_id) that can bust query concurrency and storage performance
Downstream consumers may depend on fields not included in the initial ontology leading to rework
Retention and PII classification needs coordination and could delay materialization for sensitive orgs
notes: Prefer denormalized columns for common filter predicates (region, workspace_type, plan_tier) to avoid repeated joins
Consider compaction policy: weekly small-file compaction + monthly rewrite for high-cardinality orgs
We will include provenance columns: source_event_time, ingestion_time, raw_event_path
Add a lightweight change table for last_7_days of records to support nearline dashboards without full re-materialization
